newsitem.title: UK: Weekend rain helps UK crops, but now frost feared.
newsitem.headline: Weekend rain helps UK crops, but now frost feared.

text.p: Weekend rain over southern and eastern England eased some of the concerns over parched British crops, but as the weather turned colder, frost was becoming an increasing fear for farmers.

In the 24 hours to 0600 GMT on Tuesday rainfall in the important cereals producing areas of eastern England ranged from 7-8 millimetres up to 10-12 millimetres, a spokesman for the London Weather Centre said.
Rain crossed the southern UK as an unsettled Bank Holiday weekend drew to a close.
The rain had just arrived in Kent, the spokesman said.

But the immediate worry for farmers is the frost forecast for Tuesday evening in many areas. Some barley crops, which are well forward, could be especially at risk, according to an expert at agricultural consultants ADAS.
There had already been some frost damage to crops in south-central England earlier in the season, he said.
The rain over the weekend and on Monday helped most crops get back to normal, he said. "The rain has darkened everything up," he said, as crops absorb the moisture and growth returns to normal.
"Everything should start coming through a storm now, providing this frost doesn't do too much damage," he said.
The rain was exactly what was needed. "When it rained last week we said we needed this every ten days or so, and the weather has obliged," the ADAS expert said.
Intermittent showers and cool weather are likely to continue at least until the weekend.

But the showers of the last few days and what is likely to follow, are not going to be enough to solve the long term irrigation problems of farmers, or the supply worries of domestic water providers. "You'd have to be looking at a Noah's Ark situation for it to make any difference," one water industry source said.
